supports.section: Understand the causes of layout shifts
supports.excerpt: However, because the image size isn't specified, space can't be allocated for it until the browser starts to download it and can determine its dimensions. As images load, text shifts down the page to make room for them, creating a confusing and frustrating user experience. This is where aspect ratio comes in. The aspect ratio of an image is the ratio of its width to its height. It's common to see this expressed as two numbers separated by a colon (for example, 16:9 or 4:3). For an x:y aspect ratio, the image is x units wide and y units high. This means if we know one of the dimensions, the other can be determined. For a 16:9 aspect ratio: - If puppy.jpg has a 360px height, width is 360 x (16 / 9) = 640px - If puppy.jpg has a 640px width, height is 640 x (9 / 16) = 360px Knowing the aspect ratio for an image allows the browser to calculate and reserve sufficient space for the height and associated area. Modern best practice for setting image dimensions Because modern browsers set the default aspect ratio of images based on an image's `width` and `height` attributes, you can prevent layout shifts by setting those attributes on the image and including the preceding CSS in your style sheet. ``` ``` All browsers will then add a default aspect ratio based on the element's existing `width` and `height` attributes.

skill_drafts.name: Reserve image space using aspect ratio
skill_drafts.description: Prevent layout shifts by calculating and reserving space for images before they load, using aspect ratio derived from width and height attributes. When image dimensions are known or can be derived from aspect ratio, set width and height attributes to allow the browser to pre-allocate space and avoid text reflow.
applicable_signals: Image source is specified but dimensions are missing
Aspect ratio of image is known or documented
Text or other content is positioned below the image
contraindications: Image dimensions are truly unknown and cannot be inferred
Responsive images with multiple sources (srcset) require different handling
Image is dynamically sized based on container without fixed aspect ratio
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Determine aspect ratio', 'detail': 'Identify or calculate the aspect ratio of the image (e.g., 16:9, 4:3, 1:1)'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Calculate missing dimension', 'detail': 'If one dimension is known, use the formula: missing_dimension = known_dimension × (ratio_component / other_ratio_component)'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Set width and height attributes', 'detail': 'Add width and height attributes to the tag with calculated values'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify space reservation', 'detail': 'Confirm that the browser reserves space before image download begins'}
triggers: Image dimensions are known or can be calculated from aspect ratio
Browser needs to allocate space before image download completes
Layout shift risk detected due to late-loading images
constraints: Both width and height attributes must be set on the img element
Aspect ratio must be accurately known or calculated
CSS must preserve the aspect ratio for responsive layouts
cautions: Incorrect aspect ratio calculation will result in distorted or improperly sized images
Setting only one dimension without aspect ratio CSS may not prevent layout shifts
Responsive images with srcset may require additional techniques beyond this micro-skill
output_contract: Browser reserves sufficient vertical and horizontal space for the image before download; text and other content do not shift when the image loads; layout remains stable.

examples.input: Image with 640px width and known 16:9 aspect ratio
Image with 360px height and known 16:9 aspect ratio

metadata.prompt: 1. Identify the image's aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9, 4:3). 2. If one dimension is known, calculate the other using the aspect ratio formula: for x:y ratio, if width is known, height = width × (y/x); if height is known, width = height × (x/y). 3. Set both width and height attributes on the element (e.g., ). 4. Include CSS to ensure the aspect ratio is preserved across responsive layouts. 5. Verify that space is reserved before the image begins downloading.

skill_drafts.name: Image dimension specification best practice
skill_drafts.description: Reference guide for setting width and height attributes on img elements to enable browser aspect-ratio inference and prevent cumulative layout shift.
applicable_signals: Developer or designer needs to understand modern best practice for declaring image dimensions in HTML
Layout shift issues are being investigated and root cause analysis points to unspecified image dimensions
New image markup is being created or reviewed
contraindications: Image dimensions are dynamically generated or truly variable with no static aspect ratio available
Image is responsive and dimensions change based on viewport or container width
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': "Identify the image's aspect ratio", 'detail': 'Determine the ratio of width to height (e.g., 16:9, 4:3). If one dimension is known, calculate the other using the aspect ratio formula.'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Set width and height attributes on the img element', 'detail': "Add both width and height attributes to the img tag with values that match the image's actual aspect ratio."}

{'step': 3, 'action': 'Verify browser behavior', 'detail': 'Modern browsers will automatically add a default aspect ratio based on the width and height attributes, reserving space before the image loads.'}
triggers: Developer or designer needs to understand modern best practice for declaring image dimensions in HTML.
constraints: Both width and height attributes must be present on the img element
The width and height values must reflect the actual aspect ratio of the image
cautions: Setting incorrect width and height values will distort the image or reserve wrong space
This approach works for static images; responsive images require additional CSS techniques
output_contract: Developer understands that setting width and height attributes on img elements allows modern browsers to infer aspect ratio and reserve space automatically, preventing layout shifts during image load.

examples.input: Image file puppy.jpg with 640px width and 360px height (16:9 aspect ratio)
examples.notes: Browser reserves 640×360px space before image loads, preventing text shift

examples.input: Image with known height of 360px and 16:9 aspect ratio
examples.notes: Aspect ratio allows calculation of missing dimension

metadata.prompt: Modern browsers automatically infer the aspect ratio of an image from its width and height attributes. By setting both width and height on img elements, the browser can reserve sufficient space before the image loads, preventing text and other content from shifting down the page. This is the modern best practice for preventing layout shifts caused by late-loading images.
